families.title: Stop-on-K successes with conditioned stop cause (negative hypergeometric + truncation)
families.template: A box has {R} red and {B} black cards. Cards are drawn without replacement until either {K} reds appear or {S} total draws are made, whichever happens first. You are told the process ended because {K} reds appeared (not because the draw limit was hit). What is the probability that exactly {N} draws were needed?
sampling_constraints: K <= N <= min(R+B, S)
P(stop by K reds) > 0
families.why_structured: Stopping-time definition + conditioning on stop cause + exact-time probability.

families.title: Urn with branch-dependent state update, then second-stage target
families.template: An urn starts with {R0} red and {B0} blue. You draw {d1} balls without replacement and observe {x} reds. If {x} >= {T}, you add {aR} red and {aB} blue; otherwise you remove {rR} red and {rB} blue (if possible). Then you draw {d2} balls from the updated urn. Compute P(second draw has exactly {y} red | first draw had exactly {x} red).
sampling_constraints: T is interior (some x below T, some x >= T possible in the family)
Both branches are feasible (add always feasible; remove feasible when triggered by the conditioned event)
families.why_structured: Explicit dependence (state update) + branch conditioning + second-stage hypergeometric.

families.title: Partial revelation (coarse information) then conditional probability
families.template: A deck has {R} red and {B} black cards. You draw {n} cards without replacement and only learn that the number of reds is in the set {M_SET}. Then you draw {t} more cards from the remaining deck. What is the probability that the second batch contains at least {q} red given this partial information?
sampling_constraints: M_SET must be feasible within [0, n]
Conditional event must have positive probability
families.why_structured: Conditioning on a union of events + updated composition + tail probability.

families.title: Two-source mixture with posterior after noisy test, then expected cost
families.template: A component is sourced from Supplier A with probability {pi} and Supplier B otherwise. Defect rate is {pA} for A and {pB} for B. A test returns "fail" with sensitivity {sens} and false-positive rate {fp}. You test one component; if it shows "fail," you do {r} retests and discard the component if at least {u} of all tests indicate "fail." Each test costs {cT}, discarding costs {cD}, and keeping a defective component costs {cF}. Compute the expected total cost.
sampling_constraints: pi, pA, pB, sens, fp in (0, 1)
Decision rule non-degenerate: 1 <= u <= r+1
families.why_structured: Bayes posterior + binomial aggregation + threshold decision + expected cost across outcomes.

families.title: Markov chain with absorbing barrier and reward accumulation
families.template: A token moves daily among states {0,1,2,...,L} with L={L}. From state i (1<=i<=L-1), it goes to i+1 with probability {p}, to i-1 with probability {q}, and stays with probability 1-p-q. States 0 and L are absorbing. Starting from {s}, you earn {g_expr} coins each day you are in state i (including the start day) until absorption, and then pay a one-time fee {F} if absorbed at L (otherwise 0). Compute the expected net coins.
sampling_constraints: g_expr chosen from a small parametric form (e.g., alpha*i + beta)
families.why_structured: Recursion/expected value with absorption + path-dependent reward + terminal fee.

families.title: Conditional expectation of nonlinear function of a stopping time
families.template: Independent trials succeed with probability {p}. You run trials until you obtain {k} successes, but you stop early at {S} trials if not yet reached. Let N be the number of trials actually performed. Given that you did reach {k} successes before {S}, compute E[{h}(N) | reached k before S].
sampling_constraints: Choose h so expectation exists (avoid extremely heavy nonlinearities)
families.why_structured: Truncated negative binomial + conditioning + nonlinear target.

families.title: Sequential sampling with replacement, state-dependent bonus draws
families.template: There are {C} coupon types. Each purchase yields one coupon uniformly. Whenever you obtain a new type for the first time, you immediately receive {b} bonus coupons (each uniformly random and independent). You stop when you have collected at least {m} distinct types. Compute the expected number of purchases.
sampling_constraints: Keep C moderate or enforce solver recursion/DP
families.why_structured: State-dependent process + expectation over Markov state (#distinct) + bonus cascade.

families.title: Without-replacement with midstream reshuffle rule (constraint-sensitive)
families.template: A bag contains {A} apples and {O} oranges. You draw items without replacement. After every {t} draws, if the number of apples drawn so far is at least {u}, you return {r} randomly chosen drawn items to the bag (uniform among drawn items) and continue; otherwise you discard the last {r} drawn items permanently. You stop after {S} total draws. What is the expected number of apples drawn?
sampling_constraints: Either enforce t divides S or define behavior for a final partial block
r <= t
Rules well-defined: cannot return/discard more than drawn in the relevant block
families.why_structured: Block-wise updates + branch condition + expectation with changing composition.

families.title: Two-urn transfer with conditional switch of transfer direction
families.template: Urn 1 has {R1} red and {B1} blue; Urn 2 has {R2} red and {B2} blue. You perform {m} rounds: in each round, draw one ball from each urn (without replacement within urn), compare colors; if they match you transfer {t} balls from Urn 1 to Urn 2 uniformly at random from Urn 1’s remaining contents, otherwise transfer {t} balls from Urn 2 to Urn 1. After {m} rounds, you draw {d} balls from Urn 1. Compute the probability of getting exactly {x} red.
sampling_constraints: Transfers feasible in all rounds (keep t small and urn sizes large, or define a replenish rule)
families.why_structured: Coupled system + conditional transfers + final hypergeometric.

families.title: Stratified sampling with unequal weights and post-stratum adjustment
families.template: A population has two strata: Stratum A size {NA} with mean {muA}, variance {sigmaA2}, and Stratum B size {NB} with mean {muB}, variance {sigmaB2}. You sample {nA} from A and {nB} from B without replacement. Then you discover a measurement bias: all A observations should be increased by {delta} only if the overall sample mean is below {tau}, otherwise no correction. Compute the expected corrected overall mean.
sampling_constraints: Choose parameters so the correction triggers with nontrivial probability (avoid always below/always above tau)
families.why_structured: Stratified estimator + conditional correction rule + expectation over a threshold event.

families.title: Multi-phase Poisson process with threshold-triggered rate change
families.template: Calls arrive as a Poisson process with rate {lam1} per hour for the first {T} hours. If at least {k} calls arrived in that period, the rate switches to {lam2} for the next {U} hours; otherwise it switches to {lam3}. Compute the probability that total calls over {T_plus_U} hours exceeds {M}.
sampling_constraints: lam1, lam2, lam3 > 0
Choose values so both branches occur with nontrivial probability
families.why_structured: Two-phase model + branch on first-phase count + tail probability on total.

families.title: Confidence interval width under adaptive sample size rule
families.template: You measure a process with unknown mean and known standard deviation {sigma}. You take {n0} initial samples. If the sample variance exceeds {v0}, you take an additional {n1} samples; otherwise take {n2}. Using a {one_minus_alpha} normal CI for the mean, compute the expected CI width.
sampling_constraints: Choose v0 near typical variance so both sample-size branches occur with nontrivial probability
families.why_structured: Adaptive procedure + random decision threshold + expected function of random sample size.

families.title: Two-mixture with loss, refill, and purity constraint
families.template: Tank A contains {VA} liters of solution at {cA}% solute; Tank B contains {VB} liters at {cB}%. You transfer x liters from A to B and mix thoroughly, then spill {s} liters from B. Next you add {w} liters of pure water to B and {u} liters of {cU}% solution to B. After all operations, B’s concentration is exactly {cT}%. Find x.
sampling_constraints: 0 < x <= VA (x is the unique solution implied by parameters)
spill feasible: s <= VB + x
equation has unique solution in range under printed rounding
families.why_structured: Conservation across multiple phases + loss event + final constraint equation.

families.title: Piecewise tariff + tiered discount with rounding
families.template: A service charges {a} per unit for the first {m} units, {b} per unit for the next {n} units, and {c} per unit beyond that. If total usage exceeds {U}, a discount of {d}% applies only to the portion beyond {U}; additionally, if the pre-discount bill exceeds {P}, a flat rebate {R} is subtracted. The bill is rounded to the nearest {round_unit}. Given final bill {Bill}, find the total usage.
sampling_constraints: choose parameters so the usage lies in a nontrivial tier
ensure unique usage after rounding (or explicitly ask for smallest usage consistent)
families.why_structured: Piecewise definition + threshold discount + secondary constraint + rounding.

families.title: System of equations with conditional override rule
families.template: Two numbers x and y satisfy: (i) x + y = {S}, (ii) x − y = {D} unless x exceeds {T}, in which case condition (ii) is replaced by x·y = {P}. You are told the override did occur. Find x and y.
sampling_constraints: override branch consistent and yields real solutions
choose T so only one root exceeds T (uniquely identifies x)
families.why_structured: Branch selection + coupled constraints + solving under stated branch.

families.title: Recurrence with regime switch based on threshold
families.template: A sequence starts at a0 = {a0}. For n ≥ 0, define a_{n+1} = {r1}·a_n + {c1} if a_n ≤ {T}, and a_{n+1} = {r2}·a_n + {c2} otherwise. Let N be the smallest index where a_N first exceeds {H}. Compute N and a_N.
sampling_constraints: ensure monotone growth and that crossing H happens
avoid oscillation by parameter choice
ensure the regime switch occurs (crosses T at least once)
families.why_structured: Iterative updates + piecewise dynamics + hitting-time computation.

families.title: Work-rate with efficiency drop + bonus completion clause
families.template: Worker A alone completes a job in {TA} hours and Worker B alone in {TB} hours. They work together for {t1} hours. If by then less than {p}% of the job is done, they add Worker C who works at {eC} times A’s rate; otherwise A’s efficiency drops by {d}% for the remaining time due to fatigue. Additionally, if the job finishes before {Tbonus} hours total, they receive a bonus {B} split proportional to individual hours worked. Find the total completion time and A’s bonus share.
sampling_constraints: branch is nontrivial (not finishing in first phase)
parameters avoid borderline equality at the branch threshold
bonus clause triggers deterministically (or clearly specify conditional handling)
families.why_structured: Multi-phase rates + conditional branch + proportional allocation.

families.title: Inventory with shrinkage, restock, and target margin
families.template: A store starts with {N0} units costing {c0} each. Each day for {D1} days it sells {s1} units at price {p1}; unsold inventory shrinks by {sh}% daily. Then it restocks {N1} units at cost {c1} and changes selling price to p2 for {D2} days, selling {s2} units per day (cannot exceed inventory). Given the total profit margin over the whole period is {M}% relative to total cost, find p2.
sampling_constraints: inventory nonnegative throughout
phase-2 sales feasible
p2 uniquely solvable and in realistic range
families.why_structured: State updates + shrinkage compounding + multi-phase + final global constraint.

families.title: Weighted average with constraint-dependent weights
families.template: A final score is computed from Exam E, Project P, and Quiz average Q with weights wE={wE}, wP={wP}, wQ={wQ} (summing to 1). However, if E is below {T}, the exam weight increases by {Delta} and the project weight decreases by {Delta} (quiz unchanged). A student has P={pval}, Q={qval}, and final score {F}. Given the adjustment did occur, find E.
sampling_constraints: ensure adjustment branch valid (E < T)
weights remain valid after adjustment
unique E in allowed range
families.why_structured: Conditional rule + weighted system + branch-specific equation.

families.title: Multi-currency exchange with fees and arbitrage check
families.template: You start with {X} in currency A. You exchange to currency B at rate {rAB} with fee {f1}%, then to currency C at rate rBC with a flat fee {F2} (in currency B), then back to A at rate {rCA} with fee {f3}%. If the final amount in A is {Y}, determine the missing rate rBC and state whether the cycle is profitable if rBC increases by {eps}.
sampling_constraints: avoid negative intermediate funds (B after flat fee stays positive)
solvable for rBC
perturbation check meaningful (choose eps so profitability is not trivial)
families.why_structured: Chained transformations + mixed fee types + solving and perturbation reasoning.

families.title: Piecewise linear cost minimization with constraint coupling
families.template: You must produce {Q} units using Machine 1 and Machine 2. Machine 1 cost is {a1} per unit up to {k1} units then {b1} per unit beyond; Machine 2 cost is {a2} per unit up to {k2} units then {b2} per unit beyond. Additionally, Machine 1 output cannot exceed {cap1}, and at least {min2} units must come from Machine 2. Find the minimum total cost and the optimal split.
sampling_constraints: feasible: min2 <= Q and caps allow meeting Q
prefer parameters that require case analysis (piecewise regions matter)
families.why_structured: Piecewise costs + feasibility constraints + optimization over cases.

families.title: Polynomial parameter fit with extra constraint and integer solution
families.template: A quadratic f(t)=a t^2 + b t + c satisfies f({t1})={y1}, f({t2})={y2}, and f({t3})={y3}. In addition, the vertex occurs at t={tv} (i.e., −b/(2a)={tv}) and you are told a is an integer. Find (a,b,c).
sampling_constraints: choose points consistent with integer a and unique solution
t1,t2,t3 distinct
families.why_structured: Overdetermined constraints + derived-parameter constraint + integrality.

families.title: Project schedule with precedence, overtime, and penalty threshold
families.template: A project has tasks A, B, C, D with durations dA={dA}, dB={dB}, dC={dC}, dD={dD}. Task B and C start after A; D starts after both B and C. You can pay overtime to reduce any single task by up to {r}% at cost {c} per hour reduced. If total completion time exceeds {T}, you pay penalty {P} per hour late, but if you finish at or before {T2} you receive bonus {B}. Find the minimum expected cost assuming overtime decisions are made after you learn that task C’s duration is actually dC+{Delta} (with probability {p}) otherwise dC.
sampling_constraints: both C scenarios possible: Delta>0 and 0<p<1
avoid domination by always-overtime or never-overtime by tuning thresholds/costs
use precedence makespan: dA + max(dB,dC_actual) + dD
families.why_structured: Precedence network + conditional uncertainty + optimization with thresholds.

families.title: Bin packing with tiered shipping and must-split constraints
families.template: You must ship {N} items with weights {weights}. Boxes have max capacity {Cap}. Shipping cost is {c1} per box for the first {m} boxes and {c2} thereafter, plus surcharge {S} if any box exceeds {theta} weight. Additionally, items in set {FRAGILE_SET} cannot share a box with items in {HEAVY_SET}. Find the minimum total shipping cost.
sampling_constraints: keep N moderate for exact solving
ensure feasible packing exists under capacity and incompatibility constraints
avoid trivial one-box instances (total weight > Cap)
families.why_structured: Capacity + incompatibilities + tiered cost + surcharge requiring structured casework/optimization.

families.title: Shortest path with time-dependent tolls and conditional detour
families.template: A driver travels from {Start} to {End} through a directed graph with edges: {EDGES}. If the cumulative toll paid so far exceeds {TollCap}, all subsequent tolls are discounted by {d}%. However, if the driver enters node {X} before time {tau}, edge {e_star} becomes unavailable. Find the minimum possible total cost defined as {alpha}*(total time)+{beta}*(total toll).
sampling_constraints: graph has at least two plausible routes
conditional unavailability can matter (choose tau so reaching X early/late changes availability)
toll-discount state can be triggered on some routes
families.why_structured: Dynamic constraints + coupled objective + conditional state (time and toll).

families.title: Inventory replenishment with lead time and stockout penalties
families.template: Daily demand is {d1} units for days 1–{H1}, then {d2} units for days {H1_plus_1}–{H}. You start with {I0} units, can place an order any day which arrives after {L} days with fixed ordering cost {K} plus {c} per unit ordered. Holding cost is {h} per unit per day; stockout cost is {p} per unit unmet demand (lost sales). Additionally, if inventory ever falls below {S}, you must place an emergency order of {E} units (arrives in {Le} days at premium cost {cp}). Find the minimum total cost ordering policy under these rules.
sampling_constraints: emergency rule can trigger but is not guaranteed (there exists a policy that avoids it)
keep horizon moderate for exact optimization
lead times L and Le positive
families.why_structured: State evolution + lead times + conditional forced action + cost tradeoffs.

families.title: Counting with inclusion–exclusion plus at least/exactly mix
families.template: In a class of {N} students, {a} take Math, {b} take Physics, {c} take CS. Exactly {ab} take Math and Physics, {ac} take Math and CS, {bc} take Physics and CS, and {abc} take all three. Additionally, {z} take none. Determine how many take exactly one subject and verify consistency of the data.
sampling_constraints: must satisfy inclusion–exclusion feasibility
all implied region counts nonnegative integers
z = N - |union| consistent with provided counts
families.why_structured: Multiple constraints + consistency checking + derived counts.

families.title: Flow with capacity upgrades triggered by threshold usage
families.template: A network has a single source and sink with parallel edges described by: {EDGES}. You must send {F} units. If any edge carries more than {u} units, its capacity increases by {DeltaCap} but its cost increases by {DeltaCost} for all units on that edge. Find the minimum total cost flow.
sampling_constraints: avoid trivial single-route domination
ensure threshold can be crossed in an optimal solution for some instances
flow feasibility under base/upgrade capacities
families.why_structured: Min-cost flow + nonlinearity via threshold-triggered parameter change.

families.title: Assignment with fairness constraint and penalty for imbalance
families.template: {n} workers must be assigned to {n} tasks with base costs given by COST_MATRIX={COST_MATRIX} (row i is worker i, column j is task j). Total cost is the sum of assigned costs plus penalty {lam} times the absolute difference between total assigned cost for Group 1 workers {G1} and Group 2 workers {G2}. Additionally, at least {m} tasks in set {HARD_SET} must be assigned to Group 1. Find the assignment minimizing total cost.
sampling_constraints: feasible: |G1| supports m and HARD_SET has at least m tasks
cost matrix varied (not near-constant)
families.why_structured: Assignment + group constraint + coupled penalty term.

families.title: Multi-stage counting of schedules with forbidden patterns
families.template: A conference has {D} days and {S} sessions per day. You must schedule {A} talks of type X and {B} talks of type Y. Constraints: each day must include at least {u} X talks, no two Y talks can be consecutive within a day, and the first session of each day cannot be Y if the last session of the previous day was Y. Count the number of valid schedules.
sampling_constraints: choose parameters so the count is nonzero
keep sizes moderate for DP-based counting
families.why_structured: Multiple interacting constraints + DP/state dependence across days.

families.title: Piecewise inflow/outflow with threshold-triggered rate switch
families.template: A tank initially contains {V0} liters. Inflow is {a} L/min for the first {T} minutes (then 0). Outflow is {b} L/min throughout, but if volume ever exceeds {H}, outflow increases to {b2} L/min until volume drops below {H} again. Compute the time when the volume first hits {Vtarget}, and the total amount spilled if the tank capacity is {Cap}.
sampling_constraints: ensure crossing of H occurs during inflow (trigger switch)
ensure Vtarget is reachable and Vtarget <= Cap
ensure spill can occur (Cap is below peak volume), and volume never goes negative
families.why_structured: Piecewise accumulation + state-triggered regime change + capacity constraint.

families.title: Cost integral with tiered pricing and a constraint on average rate
families.template: A machine runs for {T} hours with power consumption P(t) = {p0} + {p1}t kW. Electricity price is {c1} per kWh up to {E} kWh total usage, then {c2} beyond, and if usage during any single hour exceeds {H}, an extra surcharge {s} per kWh applies to that hour only. Compute total cost and the average price per kWh.
sampling_constraints: ensure some hours exceed the per-hour threshold H and some do not
ensure total energy crosses the tier boundary E (0 < E < total energy)
units consistent (kW integrated over hours -> kWh)
families.why_structured: Integral for energy + tiered pricing + hour-local surcharge condition.

families.title: Optimization with piecewise penalty and feasibility interval
families.template: A company chooses production level x (continuous) with revenue R(x)={R_expr} and base cost C(x)={C_expr}. The cost includes a piecewise penalty: add {p} if x<{L}, add {q}(x-{U})^2 if x>{U}, otherwise 0. Additionally, x must satisfy g1(x)={g1_expr}<=0 and g2(x)={g2_expr}<=0. Find the maximizing x and the profit.
sampling_constraints: feasible region nonempty (constraints consistent)
objective yields a unique optimum on the feasible region (concavity/strong curvature)
penalty thresholds satisfy 0 < L < U and are within the feasible range
families.why_structured: Constrained optimization + piecewise objective + multiple constraints.

families.title: Differential equation with intervention at threshold and total-dose constraint
families.template: A drug concentration follows dC/dt = -{k}C between doses. You administer {n} identical bolus doses of size {D} at scheduled times t_i=(i-1)*{Delta} hours for i=1..{n}. If concentration exceeds {H}, you skip the next scheduled dose once. The planned total dose is exactly {Total}. Given k, H, and this schedule pattern, compute the final concentration at time {Tend} and how many doses were skipped.
sampling_constraints: skipping can occur but not always (for sampled instances enforce 1 <= skipped <= ~n/2)
k>0, Delta>0, n integer >=2, Tend >= last scheduled time
Total = n*D (planned), while skip rule reduces administered doses
families.why_structured: Piecewise dynamics + threshold-triggered discrete intervention + global dose bookkeeping.

families.title: Related rates with multi-stage motion and constraint change
families.template: A ladder of length {L} slides with the bottom moving away from the wall at {v1} m/s for {T} seconds. After that, the bottom speed changes to {v2} unless the top height is below {hmin}, in which case the ladder is stopped for {S} seconds then resumes at {v2}. Find the total time until the top reaches height {h} and the total distance the bottom traveled.
sampling_constraints: target height h is achievable (0 < h < L)
ensure multi-stage behavior (typically target not reached during first phase)
stop condition can activate in some instances (hmin near the height at time T)
families.why_structured: Geometric constraint + piecewise rate change + conditional stop event.

families.title: Coordinate geometry with intersection constraint + conditional replacement
families.template: Two lines ℓ1: y={m1}x{b1_term} and ℓ2: y={m2}x{b2_term} intersect at P. A circle centered at P with radius {r} intersects the x-axis at points A and B. If |AB|<{T}, the radius is replaced by {r2}; otherwise the circle is translated by vector ({dx},{dy}). Compute the final area of the circle segment above the x-axis.
sampling_constraints: m1 != m2 so intersection exists
initial circle intersects x-axis (|y_P| < r) so AB is defined
branch can vary across instances by controlling AB relative to T
families.why_structured: Multi-step geometry + branch condition + derived quantity (segment area).

families.title: Triangle with mixed constraints (side ratio + area + altitude threshold)
families.template: A triangle has sides a,b,c with a:b = {p}:{q} and perimeter {P}. Its area is {A}. If the altitude to side a is less than {h0}, the triangle is scaled uniformly by factor {s}. Find the final side lengths and the final inradius.
sampling_constraints: ratio+perimeter+area consistent with a valid (nondegenerate) triangle
reject instances where implied solutions are non-unique under printed rounding
branch nontrivial via h0 chosen above/below the implied altitude
families.why_structured: Coupled constraints (ratio+perimeter+area) + conditional scaling + derived inradius.

families.title: Circle chord geometry with two-stage constraint update
families.template: In a circle of radius {R}, two chords have lengths {c1} and {c2} and intersect at point P inside the circle (assume P is the midpoint of chord 1). The distance from the center to chord 1 is {d1}. If P lies within {eps} of the center, chord 2 is rotated to make its distance from center {d2}; otherwise chord 1 is shortened by {Delta}. Compute the final intersection power PA·PB for chord 1.
sampling_constraints: 0 < d1 < R and 0 < d2 < R
c1,c2 <= 2R and chosen consistently with distances (optional but enforced in generator)
branch varies by sampling d1 relative to eps; ensure Delta < c1
families.why_structured: Geometric invariants + branch-dependent modification + power-of-a-point computation.

families.title: 3D volume with piecewise filling and sloshing loss
families.template: A cylindrical tank of radius {r} is initially empty and is filled with water. For the first {T1} minutes, inflow is {a1} L/min; for the next {T2} minutes it is {a2} L/min. Outflow is {b} L/min throughout. If the water height exceeds {H}, a sloshing loss of {s}% of the excess volume above height H occurs instantly at each minute mark. Find the final water height and the total lost volume.
sampling_constraints: minute discretization explicit; simulate at minute marks
ensure threshold crossing occurs (sloshing triggers) but volume never becomes negative
units consistent (liters vs geometric volume via 1 m^3 = 1000 L)
families.why_structured: Geometry-volume conversion + multi-phase rates + discrete threshold-triggered loss.

families.title: Coordinate polygon area with constraint-dependent vertex shift
families.template: A quadrilateral has vertices A({x1},{y1}), B({x2},{y2}), C({x3},{y3}), D({x4},{y4}). If its area (shoelace) exceeds {A0}, shift vertex C by vector ({u},{v}); otherwise reflect vertex D across line y={k}. Compute the final perimeter and area.
sampling_constraints: avoid self-intersection in the initial quadrilateral and after the triggered transformation
branch can vary across instances by setting A0 relative to initial area
families.why_structured: Compute area then apply transformation + recompute perimeter/area.

families.title: CRT with range constraint and digit-sum branch
families.template: Find the smallest positive integer n such that n ≡ {a1} (mod {m1}), n ≡ {a2} (mod {m2}), and n ≡ {a3} (mod {m3}). Additionally, if the digit sum of n is at least {S}, report n+{k}; otherwise report n-{k}.
sampling_constraints: choose pairwise coprime moduli (or enforce CRT consistency)
ensure k < n so n-k stays positive
choose S relative to digit_sum(n) so both branches occur across instances
families.why_structured: CRT construction + digit-sum computation + branch-dependent final output.

families.title: GCD/LCM with extra linear constraint and parity condition
families.template: Positive integers x and y satisfy gcd(x,y)={g}, lcm(x,y)={L}, and x+y={S}. Assume x≥y. Case A (x is even): you are told x is even and additionally x−y={D}. Case B (x is odd): you are told x is odd and additionally xy={P}. Under the stated case, find (x,y).
sampling_constraints: construct x=g*a, y=g*b with gcd(a,b)=1 so lcm is consistent
enforce the stated parity case of x and x≥y
avoid multiple (x,y) solutions under the stated case
families.why_structured: Factorization via gcd/lcm + additional constraint + branch on parity.

families.title: Counting integers under multiple modular exclusions with endpoint adjustment
families.template: How many integers n in the interval [{A},{B}] are divisible by {m} but not divisible by any of {d1}, {d2}, {d3}, and also satisfy n ≡ {r} (mod {k})? If the count exceeds {T}, subtract {s}; otherwise add {s}.
sampling_constraints: interval nonempty with B>A
avoid trivial zero counts unless desired
choose T near the actual count so post-processing is non-degenerate
families.why_structured: Inclusion–exclusion style filtering + congruence intersection + threshold post-processing.

families.title: Base representation with digit constraints and conditional base switch
families.template: A number N has a base-{b} representation with exactly {L} digits, digit sum {S}, and N is divisible by {m}. If no such N exists in base {b}, switch to base {b2} while keeping the same L and S. Find the smallest valid N.
sampling_constraints: ensure existence in at least one base (b or b2)
keep (L,b) small enough for DP/backtracking feasibility
sometimes enforce 'no solution in base b' to activate fallback
families.why_structured: Digit-constraint solving + divisibility constraint + conditional fallback base.

families.title: Diophantine with bounded solutions and tie-breaker rule
families.template: Find integers (x,y) satisfying {Acoef}x+{Bcoef}y={Ccoef}, with bounds {xmin}≤x≤{xmax}, {ymin}≤y≤{ymax}. If multiple solutions exist, choose the one minimizing {w1}|x|+{w2}|y|; if still tied, choose the one with larger x. Report the chosen (x,y).
sampling_constraints: ensure at least one feasible integer solution within bounds
optionally allow multiple feasible solutions so the objective/tie-break matters
families.why_structured: Linear Diophantine + feasibility filtering + optimization/tie-break.

families.title: Loan with variable APR, extra payments, and refinance trigger
families.template: A loan has principal {P0} with APR {r1}% compounded monthly for the first {M1} months, then APR becomes {r2}%. Monthly payment is {pay}. Additionally, every {k} months you make an extra payment {extra} unless the remaining balance is below {Bth}, in which case you refinance to APR {r3}% with one-time fee {F} and new monthly payment {pay2}. Compute total interest paid and the payoff month.
sampling_constraints: payments must amortize the loan (pay exceeds interest-only)
refinance trigger possible but not guaranteed across instances (sampler enforces both behaviors)
avoid extremely long payoff horizons
families.why_structured: Multi-phase amortization + conditional refinance + extra-payment schedule.

families.title: Commission + quota bonus + clawback with returns
families.template: A salesperson sells {n1} units in Phase 1 and {n2} units in Phase 2. Unit price is {p1} then {p2}. Commission is {c}% but becomes {c2}% for units sold beyond quota {Q} (counting units across both phases). Phase-2 returns are {ret} units; if returns exceed {Rth} units, a clawback of {cb}% of Phase-1 commission applies. Taxes are {t}% applied after the higher-rate quota bonus is accounted for, but before clawback. Compute final take-home pay (commission after tax and any clawback).
sampling_constraints: choose Q and returns so both threshold regimes occur across instances
avoid negative take-home unless explicitly allowed
families.why_structured: Piecewise commission + threshold + delayed conditional clawback + ordered operations.

families.title: Multi-stage recipe scaling with yield loss and rounding
families.template: A recipe uses {a} grams ingredient X, {b} mL ingredient Y, and {c} grams ingredient Z to produce {N} servings. When scaling to {S} servings, ingredient X experiences {loss}% yield loss during cooking (so you must start with more), and ingredient Y must be measured in multiples of {step} mL (rounded up). If the pre-discount total cost exceeds {Cth}, a discount {d}% applies only to ingredient Z. Given unit costs cx={cx} per gram, cy={cy} per mL, cz={cz} per gram, compute total cost and final amounts of each ingredient used.
sampling_constraints: ensure rounding matters (scaled Y not already a multiple of step)
choose Cth around pre-discount cost so discount sometimes applies across instances
keep units consistent
families.why_structured: Scaling + yield loss + rounding constraint + conditional discount.

families.title: Shipping with volumetric weight, tiered rates, and surcharge interaction
families.template: A package has actual weight {Wkg} kg and dimensions {Lcm}×{Wcm}×{Hcm} cm. Volumetric weight is (L·W·H)/{div} kg, and billable weight is max(actual, volumetric). Rate is {r1} per kg up to {K} kg and {r2} beyond, plus fuel surcharge {fs}%. Destination zone is {zone}. If destination is in {ZONE_SET}, add flat {F} unless billable weight exceeds {T}, in which case the flat fee is waived but the fuel surcharge increases by {Deltafs}%. Compute total charge.
sampling_constraints: ensure some instances billable weight is volumetric and some actual
ensure waiver condition is nontrivial across instances (billable above/below T when in-zone)
avoid invalid negative charges
families.why_structured: Max rule + tiered pricing + conditional fee/surcharge coupling.

families.title: Multi-phase production with scrap, rework capacity, and final quality constraint
families.template: A factory produces {N} items per day for {D1} days with defect rate {p1}. Defectives can be reworked at capacity {R} items/day with success probability {s}; unreworked defectives are scrapped and failed reworks are scrapped. For the next {D2} days, production increases to {N2} but defect rate becomes {p2} unless the cumulative scrap so far exceeds {Sth}, in which case defect rate reduces to {p3} due to extra inspection cost {C} per day. Find the expected number of sellable items and the expected total inspection cost.
sampling_constraints: 0<p1,p2,p3<1 and 0<s<1 with p3<p2
rework capacity R relevant (sometimes binding)
choose Sth near expected phase-1 scrap to make both regimes plausible
families.why_structured: Stateful updates across phases + capacity + threshold-triggered regime change + expectation.
